module_title: Scaling Your Business: Contracts and Legalities

lessons.title: Understanding Basic Contract Terms
lessons.body:
A contract is a legally binding agreement between two or more parties. In Spanish, it's called a contrato. When you scale your business, you'll sign contracts with suppliers, clients, landlords, and employees. Knowing key terms helps you avoid costly mistakes. 

First, parties: las partes. The offeror is el oferente, and the offeree is el aceptante. Consideration (something of value exchanged) is la contraprestaciÃ³n. For example, if you agree to buy 100 kg of cocoa from a farmer in Ghana for 500 cedis, that's a contract. 

Key clauses: 
- Objeto del contrato: purpose of the contract. 
- Plazo: term or duration. 
- Precio: price. 
- Forma de pago: payment method. 
- ClÃ¡usula de rescisiÃ³n: termination clause. 
- PenalizaciÃ³n por incumplimiento: penalty for breach. 

In many African countries, oral contracts are valid, but written contracts are safer. For cross-border deals, specify jurisdiction (jurisdicciÃ³n) and arbitration (arbitraje). For instance, 'Las partes acuerdan resolver disputas mediante arbitraje en la CÃ¡mara de Comercio de Nairobi.' 

Always check for a 'clÃ¡usula de fuerza mayor' (force majeure) to protect against unforeseen events like floods or strikes. Also, ensure both parties sign and date (firma y fecha) the document. Keep copies. If you don't understand a term, ask a lawyer or use a translation tool like DeepL. 

Practice: Write a simple contract in Spanish for a service you offer. Use at least five terms from above. This builds your vocabulary and confidence.

lessons.title: Discussing Terms and Conditions
lessons.body:
Terms and conditions (tÃ©rminos y condiciones) are the rules of your contract. When negotiating, you'll discuss these in Spanish. Start with 'Quisiera negociar los tÃ©rminos' (I would like to negotiate the terms). 

Common phrases: 
- 'Â¿EstÃ¡ de acuerdo con estas condiciones?' (Do you agree with these conditions?) 
- 'Propongo un pago del 50% por adelantado.' (I propose a 50% advance payment.) 
- 'Â¿Podemos incluir una clÃ¡usula de confidencialidad?' (Can we include a confidentiality clause?) 
- 'El plazo de entrega serÃ¡ de 30 dÃ­as.' (The delivery term will be 30 days.) 
- 'Si hay retraso, se aplicarÃ¡ una multa del 2% por semana.' (If there is a delay, a 2% penalty per week will apply.) 

In Africa, business relationships often rely on trust, but clear terms prevent disputes. For example, a Kenyan supplier might agree to deliver goods in 45 days, but if you don't specify, delays can hurt your cash flow. Always clarify: 'Â¿QuÃ© sucede si no se cumple el plazo?' (What happens if the deadline is not met?) 

Use tools like Google Translate for quick checks, but for legal documents, hire a translator. In Spanish-speaking countries like Equatorial Guinea, contracts are in Spanish, so knowing these phrases is essential. 

Practice role-play: One person is the buyer, the other the seller. Negotiate payment terms, delivery, and penalties. Record yourself and listen for accuracy. This will prepare you for real negotiations.

lessons.title: Registering a Business: Vocabulary and Phrases
lessons.body:
To scale legally, you must register your business. In Spanish, registration is 'registro de empresa' or 'constituciÃ³n de sociedad'. Common business structures: 
- Empresa unipersonal (sole proprietorship) 
- Sociedad de responsabilidad limitada (S.R.L. or LLC) 
- Sociedad anÃ³nima (S.A. or corporation) 

Steps to register in a Spanish-speaking country (e.g., Equatorial Guinea or Spain): 
1. Reserva de nombre (name reservation) at the commercial registry. 
2. Escritura pÃºblica (public deed) before a notary. 
3. NÃºmero de IdentificaciÃ³n Fiscal (NIF) or tax ID. 
4. Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry). 
5. Licencia de apertura (opening license) from the municipality. 

Key phrases: 
- 'Quiero registrar una sociedad de responsabilidad limitada.' (I want to register a limited liability company.) 
- 'Â¿CuÃ¡les son los requisitos?' (What are the requirements?) 
- 'Necesito el formulario de solicitud.' (I need the application form.) 
- 'Â¿CuÃ¡nto cuesta la inscripciÃ³n?' (How much does registration cost?) 

In many African countries, you can register online. For example, in Nigeria, the CAC (Corporate Affairs Commission) allows online registration. In Spanish-speaking countries, the process may take 1-2 weeks and cost between $200 and $1000. 

After registration, you'll get a Tax ID (NIF) and must file annual returns. Keep your registration documents safe. If you expand to another country, you may need to register a branch (sucursal). 

Practice: Look up the registration process for a Spanish-speaking country you're interested in. Write a short paragraph in Spanish describing the steps.

lessons.title: Taxes and Licenses in Spanish-Speaking Countries
lessons.body:
Taxes (impuestos) and licenses (licencias) are mandatory for scaling. In Spanish-speaking countries, common taxes include: 
- IVA (Impuesto al Valor Agregado): VAT, typically 15-21%. 
- Impuesto sobre la Renta (ISR): income tax, 25-35%. 
- Impuesto de Sociedades: corporate tax. 

You must also get licenses: licencia de funcionamiento (operating license), licencia sanitaria (health license) for food businesses, and licencia ambiental (environmental license). 

Key phrases: 
- 'Â¿DÃ³nde puedo pagar los impuestos?' (Where can I pay taxes?) 
- 'Necesito una licencia de funcionamiento.' (I need an operating license.) 
- 'Â¿CuÃ¡l es la fecha lÃ­mite para declarar impuestos?' (What is the deadline to file taxes?) 
- 'Â¿Hay exenciones para pequeÃ±as empresas?' (Are there exemptions for small businesses?) 

In Equatorial Guinea, the tax authority is 'DirecciÃ³n General de Impuestos'. In Spain, it's 'Agencia Tributaria'. In many African countries, tax rates are lower for small businesses. For example, in Kenya, small businesses with turnover below 5 million KES pay a presumptive tax. 

Always keep receipts (recibos) and invoices (facturas). Use accounting software like QuickBooks or Wave. If you're late, you may face multas (fines) and interest (intereses). 

Consider hiring an accountant (contador) to handle taxes. They cost around $100-$300 per month but save you from penalties. 

Practice: List three taxes your business would pay in a Spanish-speaking country. Write a sentence in Spanish about each.

lessons.title: Hiring Employees and Writing Job Descriptions
lessons.body:
Hiring (contrataciÃ³n) is key to scaling. In Spanish, an employee is 'empleado' and a job description is 'descripciÃ³n del puesto'. 

A job description should include: 
- TÃ­tulo del puesto (job title) 
- Funciones (duties) 
- Requisitos (requirements) 
- Salario (salary) 
- Horario (schedule) 
- UbicaciÃ³n (location) 

Example: 'Buscamos un vendedor con experiencia en ventas de productos agrÃ­colas. Debe hablar espaÃ±ol e inglÃ©s. Salario: 300.000 CFA por mes.' 

When interviewing, ask: 
- 'Â¿CuÃ¡l es su experiencia previa?' (What is your previous experience?) 
- 'Â¿Por quÃ© quiere trabajar aquÃ­?' (Why do you want to work here?) 
- 'Â¿Puede trabajar los fines de semana?' (Can you work weekends?) 

In many African countries, labor laws require written contracts (contrato de trabajo), minimum wage (salario mÃ­nimo), and social security (seguridad social). For example, in Senegal, the minimum wage is about 333 CFA per hour. In Equatorial Guinea, it's 150,000 CFA per month. 

You must also register employees for social security and pay contributions. Failure can lead to fines. 

Use platforms like LinkedIn or local job boards to post openings. For Spanish-speaking roles, specify 'Se requiere espaÃ±ol fluido'. 

Practice: Write a job description in Spanish for a position in your business. Include at least five details.

lessons.title: Practice: Review a Simple Contract in Spanish
lessons.body:
Now, let's review a simple contract in Spanish. Below is a short service contract. Read it and answer the questions.

3. Plazo: El diseÃ±o se entregarÃ¡ en 15 dÃ­as. 
4. Pago: 50% por adelantado, 50% al finalizar. 
5. Confidencialidad: El Proveedor no divulgarÃ¡ informaciÃ³n del Cliente. 
6. RescisiÃ³n: Cualquiera de las partes puede rescindir con 7 dÃ­as de aviso. 
7. Ley aplicable: Las leyes de Senegal.

Questions: 
1. Â¿CuÃ¡l es el objeto del contrato? (What is the purpose?) 
2. Â¿CuÃ¡nto es el precio total? (What is the total price?)

Answers: 1. DiseÃ±ar un logotipo. 2. 200.000 CFA. 3. 15 dÃ­as. 4. 50% adelantado, 50% al final. 5. Se puede rescindir con 7 dÃ­as de aviso. 

Now, practice with a contract from your own business. Identify key terms and translate them. Use a dictionary if needed. This exercise builds your confidence to handle real contracts in Spanish.

quiz.q: What is the Spanish word for 'contract'?
quiz.explanation: Contrato is the Spanish term for a legally binding agreement.
